claims.explanation: JZL-184 inhibits monoacylglycerol lipase (MGLL/MAGL), the enzyme that degrades 2-arachidonoylglycerol (2-AG); MAGL is overexpressed in several aggressive cancers and supports tumor growth via fatty acid oxidation and pro-tumorigenic lipid signaling (PGE2, LPA), so lines with high MAGL expression and active lipid-metabolic/oncogenic signaling are expected to be most sensitive. Conversely, low MAGL expression or dependence on alternative lipid pathways would be protective. The selective killing pattern is therefore best explained by MAGL expression levels and downstream lipid signaling rather than by any single lineage or common driver mutation.

features.basis: MAGL is the direct target; high expression predicts greater dependence and drug effect (PMID 27767105)
PTEN loss activates PI3K/AKT and lipid biosynthesis, potentially increasing dependence on MAGL-derived fatty acids; enriched in sensitive lines
TP53 mutation is common in sensitive lines and may impair stress responses, increasing reliance on lipid metabolism
KRAS-driven tumors often upregulate lipid metabolism and may depend on MAGL for fatty acid supply
BRAF-mutant melanoma lines are enriched among sensitive lines, possibly reflecting MAPK-driven lipid dependence
NF1 loss activates RAS/MAPK and may increase lipid metabolic demand; seen in several sensitive lines
RB1 loss is present in several sensitive lines and may alter metabolic dependencies
ARID1A mutations appear in multiple sensitive lines and may affect chromatin-linked metabolic programs
KMT2D mutations are enriched in least-affected lines, suggesting reduced sensitivity
EGFR-mutant lung lines appear in both groups but some are least affected, suggesting EGFR signaling may bypass MAGL dependence
PIK3CA mutations are common in least-affected lines, possibly indicating alternative lipid sources
CDKN2A loss appears in several least-affected lines, though evidence is weak
